title: Random Query
statementMd:
You are given an array $*a*$ consisting of $*n*$ positive integers. You pick two integer numbers $*l*$ and $*r*$ from $1$ to $*n*$, inclusive (numbers are picked randomly, equiprobably and independently). If $*l* > *r*$, then you swap values of $*l*$ and $*r*$. You have to calculate the expected value of the number of unique elements in segment of the array from index $*l*$ to index $*r*$, inclusive ($1$-indexed).

## Input

The first line contains one integer number $*n*$ $(1 ≤ *n* ≤ 10^{6})$. The second line contains $*n*$ integer numbers $*a*_{1}$, $*a*_{2}$, ... $*a*_{*n*}$ $(1 ≤ *a*_{*i*} ≤ 10^{6})$ — elements of the array.

## Output

Print one number — the expected number of unique elements in chosen segment.

Your answer will be considered correct if its absolute or relative error doesn't exceed $10^{ - 4}$ — formally, the answer is correct if ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/8e6753bb7c233d712f20d63937221dcfd71cab0e.png), where $*x*$ is jury's answer, and $*y*$ is your answer.
